ticket.title: gaugeblock-error: error categories and one code mapping, instead of 97 boundary sites stringifying foreign errors
acceptance_criteria:
MEASURED WITH MITER 2026-11-06, and it reverses my own earlier sequencing advice.

`miter impact BenchworkError` (depth 4) reports three sections that matter here:
  Affected tests: 6 distinct test symbols, so a refactor has a concrete verification set.
  Entrypoints and handlers: run_in_process_synthesis in xray_service, plus the daemon's whole route layer - post_claim_task_handler, post_record_handoff_handler, post_update_task_handler, post_split_task_handler, post_archive_task_handler.
  Construction sites by grep: benchwork-core 53, chalkline-core 3.

So the error type is not a leaf: it reaches the HTTP handlers, and in benchwork it is constructed in 53 places. I previously proposed benchwork-core as the natural pilot because it had the most sites; that was reasoning backwards. A pilot's job is to prove the shape cheaply and be abandoned cheaply if the shape is wrong, so it belongs in the crate with the smallest blast radius. Corrected plan:
  1. Pilot in chalkline-core (3 construction sites, no daemon, no handler layer). Convert every site in one commit.
  2. If the shape survives contact, take sawhorse or outfeed next (medium).
  3. benchwork-core last: 53 sites plus a reachable handler layer is where a wrong shape becomes expensive.
The all-or-nothing gate still holds per crate. The change is only which crate goes first.

CLONE EVIDENCE for the CLI half, with a caveat worth recording. `miter clones --min-lines 12 --similarity 0.85` puts benchwork-cli/main.rs and chalkline-cli/main.rs at 85.9 percent similarity, which is the boilerplate signal one would hope for - but the same run also pairs dado's main() with outfeed's parse_header at 85.2 percent, which is nonsense. That is GB-197 showing itself: the tool compares shape without a content dimension, so two functions that share a silhouette match even when they share nothing else. Conclusion used here: the structural similarity of the CLI entrypoints is real but this measurement is too noisy to quantify it. Direct counts are cleaner and are what the recommendation rests on.

task.title: gaugeblock-error: error categories and one code mapping, instead of 97 boundary sites stringifying foreign errors

acceptance_criteria:
MEASURED 2026-11-06, in answer to whether a common error crate is warranted. Short version: yes, but not the crate the name suggests. A universal error enum would be a mistake; a small classification layer would not.

WHAT IS ALREADY HEALTHY, so nobody deletes it:
- 28 domain error enums, each with its own variants. They are genuinely different: TaskNotFound and InvalidWorkspace and Parse are not one thing wearing three names. Merging them would produce a god-enum whose every match arm is unreachable in most crates.
- JSON-RPC codes are already centralised: gaugeblock-mcp::protocol::code (PARSE_ERROR, METHOD_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PARAMS). A grep for literal "-326xx" codes in the seven *-mcp crates finds nothing, so that duplication does not exist yet.
- Exit codes are barely a problem today: two process::exit sites in the whole suite, and anyhow at the binary boundary does the rest.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is one thing: 97 boundary sites flatten a foreign error into a string.
  BenchworkError::Storypole(e.to_string())     ChalklineError::Storypole(e.to_string())
  BenchworkError::Workspace(e.to_string())     OutfeedError::Storypole(e.to_string())
The variants even name the product that failed - Storypole(String) appears 3 times, Sawhorse(String) twice - which is a taxonomy trying to exist inside String payloads. What is lost at each site: the error's own type, its category, its source chain, and any structure a caller could match on. What survives is prose.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW, not as tidying: three features in flight all need the same classification and each would otherwise invent it.
  gaugeblock-cli (GB-298) needs a policy mapping error to exit code.
  The MCP loop (GB-297) needs error to JSON-RPC code, and already has codes but no way to pick one from an arbitrary error.
  Telemetry (GB-294) needs status error plus the first diagnostic line, which is exactly what the stringified boundary keeps and the structured one discards.

PROPOSED SHAPE - a classification, not a replacement:
1. An ErrorCategory with a closed set: NotFound, InvalidInput, Unavailable, ExternalTool, Io, Internal. Each crate keeps its enums and adds one fn category(&self).
2. A Foreign payload type { product: &'static str, message: String, source: Option<Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> } to replace the e.to_string() variants, so a boundary records WHICH product failed and keeps the chain. Adoption is mechanical: Foreign::from_error("storypole", e).
3. One mapping table, error category to exit code and to JSON-RPC code, owned once and referenced by gaugeblock-cli and gaugeblock-mcp. gaugeblock-mcp already has the constants; this gives them a chooser.

ZERO DEPENDENCIES. Not serde, not thiserror, nothing. 28 crates would depend on it and a foundation crate that drags a serializer into a parser is a cost paid everywhere for a benefit used in three places.

RISK, stated because it decides whether to start: a half-adopted error layer is worse than none - it produces a third representation alongside the enum variants and the strings. The gate to accept is per crate and all-or-nothing: convert every boundary site in one crate in one commit, or do not start that crate. benchwork-core alone has 38 construction sites, so it is the natural pilot and the natural proof.

Sequencing: after GB-298 exists to consume the category (otherwise this is a refactor with no customer), and before GB-297 needs to pick a JSON-RPC code. It does not block either.
